messages:
katie: Heads-up — after the 535.12 driver push to the H100 pool we're seeing a 20-40% tail-latency regression on many 512/1024 seq jobs :eyes:

sam: Confirmed. Perf traces point at a different attention kernel being chosen for a lot of requests (same model + batch shape). Looks like kernel selection hit a 'safe' fallback on H100s.

mikhail: Got a short profile excerpt — the autotuner decided on attn_generic_v1 instead of attn_h100_fused for seq=512. That generic path does extra memcopies + serialized loops.

nina: Repro steps I used:
```
# run one-shot perf harness on an h100 node
python perf_harness.py --model redwood-xl --seq 512 --batch 4 --profile
# observed kernel picks printed in logs
```
Output snippet: 
```
kernel_pick: attn_generic_v1 (score 0.63)
kernel_pick_expected: attn_h100_fused (score 0.61)
note: chosen path increases host->device staging buffers
```

sam: Interesting that score was lower but chosen — suspect driver/cuBLAS changed timings so the autotuner's cached timings are stale. The tuner picks based on microbenchmarks done at build time and an on-disk cache.

katie: Quick mitigation idea: set REDWOOD_AUTOTUNER_MODE=safe to force only vetted kernels, or set REDWOOD_KERNEL_BLACKLIST to block attn_generic_v1 while we triage. Both are hot-config flags.

mikhail: Blacklist sample (Kubernetes env):
```yaml
env:
  - name: REDWOOD_KERNEL_BLACKLIST
    value: "attn_generic_v1,matmul_scalar_fallback"
  - name: REDWOOD_AUTOTUNER_MODE
    value: "safe"
```

nina: Another quick workaround: reduce per-worker BATCH_MAX_TOKENS to avoid hitting the path that triggers the fallback (we saw it flip once batch_tokens > 1024). Not ideal but buys time.

infra-bot: @katie detected node-pool upgrade event: driver_version=535.12 applied to pool=prod-h100-2 at 2026-03-15T02:12:43Z

sam: Rollback plan options:
- short: pin driver to 530.x and rollout nodegroup rollback ASAP (less risky)
- medium: blacklist offending kernels + set autotuner=safe to protect latency while we replay autotuner microbenchmarks against 535.x and rebuild cache
- long: make autotuner include driver/cuBLAS version in its cache key & add CI gate for driver upgrades

katie: I'm +1 for short+medium: rollback nodepool first to stop user impact, then enable blacklist + safe-mode to stabilize before attempting to re-run autotuner on a staging pool with 535.x.

mikhail: Commands I used to repro and re-tune locally:
```
# run the microbench harness that autotuner uses
./tools/kernel_microbench --device h100 --driver 535.12 --out microbench_535.json
# compare to baseline
./tools/compare_microbench baseline.json microbench_535.json
```
We should add that as part of the driver-upgrade checklist.

deploy-bot: Starting nodegroup rollback for prod-h100-2 -> previous image driver=530.41 (in progress) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

nina: Post-mortem items I noted: autotuner cache TTL is effectively infinite; we need an invalidation hook when infra-level libs (driver/cuBLAS/cudnn) change. Also kernel selection heuristics should prefer "same-arch optimized" kernels when scores are within noise margin.

sam: Also saw subtle KV-cache behavior differences: under the generic kernel path we end up performing a sync of KV into host memory at longer seq lengths, which hurts long-chat flows. That suggests we should add a runtime check to avoid kernel switches mid-session (pin per-connection kernel choice).

katie: TL;DR action list:
- infra: finish rollback (katie + infra)
- runtime: enable REDWOOD_KERNEL_BLACKLIST + REDWOOD_AUTOTUNER_MODE=safe in prod rollout (sam, nina)
- eng-ml: run autotuner full re-bench on 535.x in staging and publish delta (mikhail)
- infra/governance: add driver/cuBLAS version to autotuner cache key + driver-upgrade CI gating (katie)

mikhail: Adding one more note — we should treat driver upgrades like ABI changes: bump a manifest version so runtime can opt to invalidate caches automatically.

katie: Thanks all — will post a short runbook in #incidents once the rollback completes. :thumbsup:
